chunks: Thus, we are superior firstly because of kinship and secondly because of obedience. When at Saqīfah the muhājirūn contended kinship with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) against the anṣār, they scored over them. If that success was based on kinship then the right would be ours better than yours. Otherwise, the anṣar’s contention stands.
ai.seo_question: How does the argument of kinship at Saqifah support the claim of Ahl al-Bayt to leadership?
ai.summary: Imam Ali employs a dialectical strategy by accepting the Muhajirun's premise at Saqifah—that kinship with the Prophet confers precedence—to demonstrate that the Ahl al-Bayt hold the strongest claim to authority. This passage underscores the Shia theological principle that political legitimacy is intrinsically linked to spiritual and familial proximity to the Prophet, contrasting with the Sunni historical narrative that prioritized consensus (shura). By invoking the Saqifah debate, Ali highlights the continuity of divine selection through the Prophet's lineage rather than mere tribal affiliation.
